_comment: The Book of Shadows: The Mage Players Guide (White Wolf) as a byo-rulebook module. Ships structure and citations only. This is where Mage 2nd Edition's Merits and Flaws actually live — they are NOT in the core rulebook, as that book's own index confirms (no 'Merits' entry between Methodologies and Mistridge, no 'Flaws' between First Cabal and Foci).

source.title: The Book of Shadows: The Mage Players Guide
source.text_layer_note: Image-only scan: pdftotext over all 210 pages yields zero characters, exactly as with the core rulebook. Every locator here is therefore 'manual'. page_offset 1 was calibrated from the page numbers the book prints on itself (PDF 31 = printed 30, PDF 47 = printed 46), NOT from the contents page, which would have given 2 and put every citation one page out.

tables.title: Merits and Flaws
tables.note: Eighteen pages of headed prose entries, not a ruled table — each entry is a heading of the form 'Name: (N pt Merit)' followed by a paragraph. Only name, cost, type and category are recorded; the descriptions are the book's prose and are deliberately not reproduced. Cost is a label because many entries are ranges ('1-5') and one, Spirit Magnet, is both a Merit and a Flaw with different ranges for each. Categories: Psychological, Mental, Awareness, Aptitudes, Supernatural, Mage Ties, Sleeper Society, Physical.

tables.title: How Merits and Flaws are bought
tables.note: Printed as an introductory passage rather than a chart; split into rules here so the freebie-point arithmetic can be checked. The seven-point Flaw cap is the one that matters mechanically — it puts a hard ceiling of 22 on freebie points.
